papers.title: Large-scale validation of an automatic EEG arousal detection algorithm using different heterogeneous databases
papers.one_line: Single-EEG + chin-EMG automatic arousal detector validated on 2768 PSGs (κ 0.56–0.60 vs clinical, ≈ human inter-scorer); algorithm details are in Alvarez-Estevez 2017 and github.com/bigsasi/arousals-detection.

papers.title: The breathing cycle gates memory reactivation during human NREM sleep
papers.one_line: Respiration-locked closed-loop TMR (N = 25 healthy, non-SDB adults) shows cues at the SO-spindle-favoured respiratory phase improve associative memory and tighten spindle nesting in SO up-states versus antiphase cues, which delay reactivation ~2 s to a later SO-spindle complex at a similar respiratory phase; also replicates endogenous respiration-SO/spindle phase coupling (SOs ~-82 deg, spindles ~+48 deg re inhalation peak).

papers.title: Combining machine learning models for the automatic detection of EEG arousals
papers.one_line: Signal-processing candidates (θ/α/>16 Hz power vs 10 s baseline ×1.5, chin EMG p2p vs 30 s baseline ×2, ≥3 s) + supervised classifiers on SHHS (sens ~0.8, spec ~0.88); ML stage needs labelled arousals, so only the front-end is usable on DREAMT.

papers.title: A simple and robust method for the automatic scoring of EEG arousals in polysomnographic recordings
papers.one_line: Rule-based single-EEG + chin-EMG + ECG arousal detector (alpha >2.5× / beta >2× 10-s baseline, EEG/EMG pattern extension, AASM-based false-positive removal); κ 0.775 on 22 clinical PSGs. The algorithm to port for DREAMT.

papers.title: Respiration modulates sleep oscillations and memory reactivation in humans
papers.one_line: In 20 healthy nappers, SOs, fast spindles and SO-spindle complexes cluster around the inhalation peak (thermistor, 0° = inhalation), and stronger respiration–SO_spindle coupling predicts memory reactivation.

papers.title: Addressing wearable sleep tracking inequity: a new dataset and novel methods for a population with sleep disorders
papers.one_line: Introduces DREAMT: concurrent Empatica E4 and clinical PSG from 100 Duke sleep-clinic patients (mean AHI 22.1/h, 40 reported snorers) plus a GPBoost+LSTM wake detector; PSG acquisition and scoring details are sparse.
